children: U.S. STOCKS END LOWER; CHIP STOCKS HAVE BIGGEST DAILY DROP SINCE JULY 1
The three major U.S. stock indexes ended lower on Monday, with technology
leading declines following a selloff in chip stocks.
finished down 5.9% in its biggest daily percentage decline since July 1.

image.alt: Chipmakers' growing weight in the S&P 500

children: Weighing on sentiment were comments over the weekend from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, calling on AI companies to slow the pace at which they advance model capabilities. OpenAI and xAI leaders also warned of risks from rapid development.
Adding to caution on Monday, the 10-year Treasury yield
hit the 5% mark for the first time since October 2023. Expectations for a U.S. rate hike rose after last week's consumer price data and recent gains in oil prices.
Traders are pricing in a 90% chance that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates by 25 basis points at its policy meeting on Wednesday, according to the CME's FedWatch tool.
Among the day's gainers were communication services
, with an index of biotech shares
also ending higher on the day.
Here is the closing market snapshot:
Main US indexes modestly red, but Nasdaq well off worst levels
Tech weakest S&P 500 sector; comm svcs leads gainers
Dollar rallies; US crude up ~2%; bitcoin gains >2%; gold down >1%
